Summary Description: Roi Docampo is a mathematician at the University of Oklahoma whose research sits at the intersection of arc-space geometry, commutative algebra, and birational geometry. He co-authored foundational work with C. Chiu and T. de Fernex on embedding codimension of arc spaces, formal embeddings, and their connections to Drinfeld–Grinberg–Kazhdan (DGK) decompositions and Mather–Jacobian discrepancies, delivering sharp bounds and a unified view of the local structure of arc spaces. He contributed to understanding the finiteness properties and ramification phenomena of arc fibers under morphisms, and to the Nash blow-up program through explicit descriptions of differential sheaves on arcs and jets. In collaboration with Tommaso de Fernex, he developed a comprehensive framework for Nash transformations of jet components, yielding relative compactifications and deteminantal constructions that formalize how morphisms extend to jet spaces. He also co-authored work with Greg Muller on juggler’s friezes, extending SL(k)-frieze theory into the Grassmannian/positroid setting via π-unimodular matrices, dualities, and Grassmannian parametrizations. Across these works, Docampo demonstrates a consistent emphasis on explicit, constructive frameworks that synthesize non-Noetherian algebra with geometric invariants, yielding practical tools for analyzing arc spaces, jet schemes, and their singularities, while also engaging combinatorial geometry through the juggler’s frieze program. His research has clear implications for arc-space singularities, Nash problems, and Mather invariants, and it reflects a broad and integrative approach to modern algebraic geometry.
